kind: Authored same-body placebo audit of native mask-width crossover
normalization: Strip instruction addresses; replace absolute branch targets with their demangled symbol+relative offset. Preserve every mnemonic, operand, register, stack access and alignment instruction.
conclusion: An unchanged raw32 10B active16/256-bucket loop changes from 4.6563 to 6.8811 ns when only the other arm mask changes from 64 to 32 bits. Serial changes from 19.3672 to 19.3195 ns.
An unchanged composed32 6B active16/256-bucket loop changes from 3.9224 to 6.1745 ns when only the other arm mask changes from 32 to 64 bits.
These placebo effects falsify mask-width backend work as a sufficient explanation and show that a fixed bucket encoding does not impose the observed ranking.
Identical loop bodies move to different code addresses. This strongly implicates placement-sensitive frontend or branch behavior; the exact microarchitectural cause remains unmeasured.
No native PMU counters or allocation-address census were collected. Do not claim a specific branch-predictor alias, I-cache mechanism, or exclude every placement-correlated data effect.
Serial and unchanged-body throughput must remain separate. No 32/64-bit production choice follows from this experiment.
This crossover uses AVX2 only. The earlier native AVX-512 6B loss has been audited statically but is not directly explained by this control.
selection: All forty same-body comparisons retained; selected placebo timings cover active1/15/16, both row widths, both footprints and hits/serial/updates. All other tails and operations remain in adjacent paired.csv and original archive.
